cf.title: [PG19]Three bugs with a CHECK constraint that only the child enforces

input.subject: [PG19] Three bugs with a CHECK constraint that only the child enforces

verdict_reasoning: v5-0001 is committed and no objection to it survived. For v5-0002 and v5-0003, standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2 survived: the dump makes the child's constraint local, and ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED would set conislocal for plain inheritance only. Message #14 leaves the plain inheritance case open and nobody answered. The goal is a valid bug fix, but the list has not agreed on this design.

brief.title: Fix three bugs with CHECK constraints only the child enforces
brief.problem: In 19, a CHECK constraint can be ENFORCED on an inheritance child or partition while the parent keeps it NOT ENFORCED. Three paths lose that state: ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on the parent marks it validated over a NOT VALID child, ALTER COLUMN TYPE recreates the child's constraint from the parent, and pg_dump restores the child as NOT ENFORCED. The first can return wrong query results through constraint exclusion.
brief.proposed_design: v5-0001 makes ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a parent fail when a child holds the constraint as ENFORCED NOT VALID, with the error ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT already raises. v5-0002 and v5-0003 make pg_dump emit the child's ENFORCED CHECK as a local constraint when no parent enforces it. The ALTER COLUMN TYPE fix moved to a separate WIP patch from jian he.
user_visible_surface: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a parent now errors when a child's constraint is ENFORCED NOT VALID, with an errhint.
pg_dump output now creates a child's ENFORCED CHECK inline in CREATE TABLE when its parents keep it NOT ENFORCED.
After restore, such a child constraint has conislocal = true, so dropping the parent's constraint no longer drops it.
author_claims: Bug 1 is new in 19, and 0001 belongs on the 19 open items list.
Bugs 2 and 3 also exist in 18; jian he says bug 2 goes back to at least 14.
pg_upgrade keeps the child ENFORCED today; only pg_dump loses it.
jian he says the local-constraint dump avoids an extra full scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock at restore.
v5-0003 skips NOT VALID constraints, because restoring one would mark it valid without a scan.
brief.thread_state: Andrew Dunstan committed v5-0001 on 2026-11-01 to close the 19 open item; v5-0002 and v5-0003 are left for later discussion. The open question is whether pg_dump may turn an inherited constraint into a local one, which jian he accepts for partitions but doubts for plain inheritance.
unclear: No consensus is shown on changing conislocal in dumps for regular inheritance versus partitions.
The thread does not say whether v5-0002 and v5-0003 would be back-patched to 18, or how.
Nobody answered Chao Li's question whether ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED should validate at all; he plans a v20 thread.
The CommitFest entry still says Needs review and does not record the commit of 0001.
Related bugs (convalidated dump loss since 14, NOT NULL restore failure in 18) have no separate thread linked yet.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"
prior_attempts.quote: pg_dump cannot currently dump all the structures that are allowed by this patch.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 0413a556990ba628a3de8a0b58be020fd9a14ed0.

pg_dump cannot currently dump all the structures that are allowed by
this patch.  This needs more work in pg_dump and more test coverage.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P12 reverted a new feature because pg_dump could not dump the inheritance states it allowed. Here the child-enforced state can already be created in 18, so the feature stays and pg_dump is changed.

prior_attempts.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
prior_attempts.quote: We have already discovered with the previous attempt that there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage. Also, there isn't even a patch yet.
prior_attempts.reason: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 changed how inherited per-table settings merge and was returned after new dump failures appeared. This proposal is a bug fix with tests, though the thread also keeps finding related dump bugs.

objections.title: Dump and pg_upgrade turn an inherited child CHECK into a local one
objections.failure_scenario: A user dumps and restores, or runs pg_upgrade on, a database where child k enforces parent p's NOT ENFORCED check c. Later the user runs alter table p drop constraint c. Before the upgrade this dropped k's copy; after it, k keeps c as a local constraint and rejects rows, and the user finds out only when inserts into k fail.
objections.argument: v5-0002 and v5-0003 emit the child's constraint inline, so it comes back with conislocal = true (messages #7, #14). Message #7 notes that pg_upgrade keeps the constraint inherited today and would stop doing so, which makes a dump fix change catalog state for upgrades that currently work. jian he doubts this is right for plain inheritance (message #14), and nobody else has agreed to it. The v1-0003 design (alter constraint ... enforced after the parent) keeps conislocal intact, at the cost of a scan at restore time.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a lossy conislocal change at restore and pg_upgrade better than the v1-0003 alter constraint form, at least under --binary-upgrade where no scan is needed?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: Message #14 leaves the conislocal change for plain inheritance open, and nobody answered before 0002 and 0003 were deferred. The notnull_islocal case in message #12 is existing practice but did not settle it; [P12] must not be used as support.

objections.title: ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED on a child would detach it from the parent
objections.failure_scenario: On a plain inheritance child, a user runs alter table k3 alter constraint c enforced and then alter table p3 drop constraint c. Under v5-0002 the child keeps c as a local constraint, but a partition in the same situation loses it. If this is back-patched to 18, a minor release changes what existing scripts do.
objections.argument: v5-0002 touches tablecmds.c and, following message #10, makes alter constraint ... enforced set conislocal for regular inheritance but not for partitions. That gives one command two meanings depending on the inheritance kind, and makes a property-change command alter inheritance linkage, which is a different job. The precedent cited in message #10 (SET NOT NULL changing conislocal) is a single case, and message #12 calls the current state an inconsistency. The thread does not say whether this change goes to 18.
objections.author_must_show: Should alter constraint ... enforced change conislocal at all, why only for plain inheritance, and is this behaviour change intended for a back-patch to 18?

critic.reasoning: v5-0002 touches tablecmds.c, and message #10 says it makes ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED set conislocal for plain inheritance only; no one agreed to that. The back-patch part does not apply, because 18 has no ALTER CONSTRAINT for CHECK (message #1).

refuted.title: Dump turns inherited child CHECK into local, diverging from pg_upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A user dumps and restores a database where child k enforces an inherited CHECK that parent p keeps NOT ENFORCED. Later, alter table p drop constraint c leaves c on k, because restore made it local. The same cluster moved with pg_upgrade drops it, so the outcome depends on how the cluster was moved.
refuted.argument: v5-0002 and v5-0003 make conislocal = true after restore. Message #7 shows pg_upgrade keeps it false, so the two paths give different catalogs. Message #14 doubts this is right for plain inheritance and asks for other opinions, and nobody answered. In [P12], a feature allowed structures pg_dump could not reproduce, and the commit was reverted. That reason points to another fix: restrict what ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED allows on an inherited child, so pg_dump does not have to rewrite catalog state.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is changing conislocal on restore better for plain inheritance than limiting ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on an inherited child, and who agreed to that trade-off?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. [P12] reverted a new feature, but the child-enforced state can already be created in 18 (message #1), so limiting ALTER CONSTRAINT would not remove it.

refuted.title: pg_upgrade would silently turn inherited child constraints into local ones
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA runs pg_upgrade on a cluster where a child enforces a CHECK that its parent keeps NOT ENFORCED. The child's pg_constraint row comes back with conislocal = true. Months later `alter table p drop constraint c` leaves the child's copy in place, and nobody can tell why it differs from the old cluster.
refuted.argument: Message #7 says pg_upgrade keeps this constraint inherited today, and that the local-constraint approach makes it local in pg_upgrade too. v5-0003 takes that approach, and the patch prose does not exclude the --binary-upgrade dump. pg_upgrade is expected to carry catalog state over unchanged. Message #14 accepts the conislocal change for partitions but leaves plain inheritance open.
refuted.author_must_show: Does v5-0002 or v5-0003 change conislocal in --binary-upgrade output, and if so, why should pg_upgrade alter catalog state it preserves today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers the pg_upgrade path and asks the same --binary-upgrade question.

refuted.title: v5-0002 changes the catalog effect of a DDL command, which conflicts with a back-patch
refuted.failure_scenario: If v5-0002 goes to 18, children enforced before the minor release keep conislocal = false and children enforced after it get conislocal = true. The same `alter table p drop constraint c` then cascades to some children and not to others. Users find out only when a parent constraint is dropped.
refuted.argument: Message #10 describes v5-0002 as making ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a child set conislocal for regular inheritance but not for partitions. That is a server behaviour change, beyond pg_dump. The brief says the thread does not settle whether v5-0002 and v5-0003 go back to 18. Existing clusters already hold the old form, so pg_dump has to handle both forms for good.
refuted.author_must_show: Is v5-0002 meant for 18, and how do clusters that already hold conislocal = false rows end up consistent with rows created after the change?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a CHECK in 18, but message #1 says that command is new in 19 and that the patches using it do not apply to 18. The remaining point about server behaviour duplicates standards-compat-2.

refuted.title: v5-0002 changes backend conislocal semantics for plain inheritance only
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs alter table k3 alter constraint c enforced on a plain inheritance child, then later runs alter table p3 drop constraint c. The child keeps its copy because conislocal was flipped, while a partition in the same situation loses it. The user finds out only when the constraint is still there.
refuted.argument: v5-0002 touches tablecmds.c and makes ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED flip conislocal for table inheritance but not partitions (message #10), so a pg_dump fix also changes server DDL behavior. jian he doubts this for regular inheritance (message #14). Message #7 notes that pg_upgrade would also turn the constraint local. If the fix goes to 18, a released branch changes DROP CONSTRAINT cascade behavior without its own discussion.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED change conislocal for inheritance children but not for partitions, and is that change meant to be back-patched to 18?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which makes the same point about ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED changing conislocal for plain inheritance only.

refuted.title: Per-property special cases in pg_dump with no general rule
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds another per-child constraint property, or changes NOT NULL handling. Nobody adds the matching local-ification case in pg_dump, and the child silently comes back with its parent's state after restore. No test fails until a user restores a dump.
refuted.argument: The thread found several dump losses of the same kind: enforced, convalidated since 14, multi-parent NO INHERIT, and NOT NULL restore failure (messages #8, #11, #12). Each needs its own branch in pg_dump, like the notnull_islocal case in flagInhAttrs that message #12 quotes. v5-0003 also skips NOT VALID constraints, so its coverage is partial. [P12] was reverted because pg_dump could not dump all structures the server allowed.
refuted.author_must_show: What single rule decides when pg_dump emits an inherited constraint as local, and which test fails if a future constraint property breaks that rule?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on an unnamed future constraint property, and the other dump losses in messages #8 and #12 predate this patch. v5-0003 states its rule, follows the flagInhAttrs pattern, and moves pg_dump toward what [P12] asked for.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Message #7 says the local-constraint dump would also make the child's constraint local under pg_upgrade, which keeps it inherited today.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: After restore the child's pg_constraint row has conislocal = true; v5-0002 also changes tablecmds.c.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a parent now errors over an ENFORCED NOT VALID child; v5-0002 changes its effect on a child.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: v5-0001 stops a parent being marked validated over a NOT VALID child, which constraint exclusion relied on.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: v5-0002 and v5-0003 change how pg_dump emits a child's ENFORCED CHECK whose parents keep it NOT ENFORCED.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Bugs 2 and 3 also exist in 18, and the thread does not say whether or how the pg_dump fixes go there.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: pg_dump gains another case that rewrites inherited constraint state, next to the not-null case from message #12.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Do v5-0002 or v5-0003 change conislocal in --binary-upgrade output, where pg_upgrade keeps the constraint inherited today?
For plain inheritance, why is restoring the child's constraint as local better than the v1-0003 form, which emits ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED after the parent?
Should ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED on a child set conislocal at all, and why for plain inheritance but not for partitions?
How will 18 get a fix for the pg_dump loss, given that v5-0002 and v5-0003 use ALTER CONSTRAINT syntax that 18 does not have?
Which thread will carry the ALTER COLUMN TYPE fix and the related dump losses from messages #8, #11 and #12?

committability.owner_note: Andrew Dunstan committed v5-0001. The pg_dump patches need a committer who knows the inheritance handling in pg_dump and the conislocal rules in tablecmds.c; none has yet spoken on them in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for how dump, restore and possibly pg_upgrade set conislocal on inherited CHECK constraints, in 19 and in any back branch. Restored clusters keep that catalog state for good.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revisions up to v5 within about a month and reworked the design after review, so follow-up looks likely.

priority.reason: The bug affects only users whose child enforces a CHECK that the parent keeps NOT ENFORCED, but for them a restore silently loses enforcement. The two remaining patches are small; the conislocal question for plain inheritance needs an answer before code review.

provisional_note: The code was not read. Whether v5-0002 and v5-0003 change --binary-upgrade output, and what exactly v5-0002 changes in tablecmds.c, is known only from thread messages.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
matched_queries: ALTER COLUMN TYPE recreates child constraint
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.
matched_queries: ALTER COLUMN TYPE recreates child constraint
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't sound like the right approach; in particular, it won't really
help for deciding whether to propagate a DROP NOT NULL on a parent rel to
its children.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: fix NOT NULL constraint name comparison using makeObjectName
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves makeObjectName and pg_encoding_mbcliplen into src/common so that pg_dump can rebuild the server's truncated auto-generated NOT NULL constraint names. pg_dump would then match names longer than 63 bytes and omit the redundant CONSTRAINT clause for domains and table columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after finding that the claimed round-trip bug does not exist. pg_dump emits the name stored in pg_constraint, which the server has already truncated, so the restored constraint keeps the same name and only a redundant CONSTRAINT clause remains. The author judged that moving makeObjectName to src/common was too much work for that. No reviewer commented on the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So the decision is wrong, but the only consequence is that a name that could have been left out is written in a CONSTRAINT clause, which is functionally harmless, and the comment above determineNotNullFlags() already says as much.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: refactor AlterDomainAddConstraint (alter domain add constraint)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes alter domain ... add constraint reject constraint options that domains do not support (NO INHERIT, NOT ENFORCED, deferrability) with domain-specific error messages. It also removes dead code in AlterDomainAddConstraint().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut committed the dead-code removal, and Alvaro Herrera's last message called the v5 patch a reasonable implementation, ugly though it is, and suggested checking deferrability before calling processCASbits(). No later message appears before the entry was returned with feedback in April 2026.
matched_queries: ALTER COLUMN TYPE recreates child constraint

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

roaster_notes.note: v5-0001 is committed (message #16) and was not challenged. The one objection covers the open pg_dump conislocal question in v5-0002 and v5-0003.
v5-0001 is committed and its error matches the existing ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT error, so I raise no objection to it. The ALTER COLUMN TYPE fix has moved to another thread and is not evaluated here.
v5-0001 is committed and adds only an error path, with no on-disk, WAL or catalog-format change. The objections cover the open v5-0002 and v5-0003.

The proposal fixes how CHECK constraint state (enforced, validated, conislocal) is kept across ALTER CONSTRAINT, ALTER COLUMN TYPE and pg_dump. It adds no new privilege, role, function or setting, and it does not change who can run these commands, which already need table ownership. The wrong-result bug in 0001 is a correctness issue for the table owner's own data. It does not let one role see or change rows it could not reach before, so I see no security or privilege angle to object on.
v5-0001 is committed and draws no objection from this angle; the objections concern only v5-0002 and v5-0003.

These are bug fixes for state that dump and restore lose; no existing feature, option or extension keeps a child-only ENFORCED CHECK through pg_dump. The local-constraint dump in v5-0003 follows the not-null precedent in flagInhAttrs (message #12), so it extends existing practice and adds no second mechanism.

These are correctness fixes, so the demand test does not apply. Bug 1 gives wrong query results through constraint exclusion. Bug 3 makes a dump and restore silently drop ENFORCED on a child's CHECK, and that hits every user of the 19 per-child enforceability feature. The bugs came from tool-assisted analysis, not field reports, but a fix for wrong results needs no demand evidence. Whether pg_dump may turn conislocal from false to true for plain inheritance is a design question for another angle.
